tasks.title: Plain JSON validation regains baseline CPU performance and rejects inherited array elements
tasks.spec: ## Repository: contract, Behavior in full (required behavior 1-5, test-first steps 1-3 and the CPU script), Files, Checks and Completion evidence; ## Counterexamples 1-13 and CPU statistic; ## Security impact, ## Non-goals and ## Rollout order. Implement the compiled schema walk, record plainness safe fallback and per-call record globals check, top-level ownValue read, Proxy test/comment change, docs, version 1.7.1 and regenerated build output together. The bench test changes only if its fixture shapes move into the CPU script; README changes only if it repeats the own-data or Proxy rule on the implementation branch. Include any other dist file regenerated by the build. If the branch already rejects cases 1-2 and parses certified plain JSON without copying, request the hold specified in Behavior rather than proceeding to review.

acceptance.expected: Bun reports 1.4.0; installation exits 0 with the existing lockfile. zod stays pinned to 4.6.7 as the only runtime dependency; no tooling, dependency, schema, type, public export or WIRE_VERSION change.

Test-first evidence on unchanged source at 7ce23aaf3fa3e038f65ecfed755188b83bde143f, after adding counterexamples: cases 1 and 2 are red because top-level inherited elements are accepted. Case 1 includes uptime and latency. Cases 3, 4, 9, 11 and 13 and guards 5-8, 10 and 12 pass. Each case uses exported validators and the literal errors, verdicts, identities and counts in Counterexamples. Record the failing test names and assertions in the PR.

Historical-walk red evidence: temporarily apply exactly the Counterexamples recipe to 7ce23aa, copying ebcbbb6 src/validate.ts lines 189-312 except the duplicate lookupGetter at 195-197, enabling isOwnData in problem and leaving arrayProblem unchanged. Run the full suite, including admin and tokens. New cases 1-4, 9 and 13 fail; each of 13a-c returns ok:true with getter count 1 instead of 0. Existing red tests are the eight admin tests named in Verified state (original lines 397, 465, 510, 559, 637, 662, 689, 710), tokens 'array elements count only as own data properties' (283), the old descriptor/get Proxy test (313, if not yet replaced), and smoke 'dist matches a fresh build of src' for the unbuilt source. The replacement Proxy test may pass. Guards 5-8, 10 and 12 pass. Record the actual failing names, compare with Behavior step 2 and report any additional existing failure. Revert the temporary walk before implementing; never commit it.

acceptance.command: bun test test/validate.test.ts test/http-options.test.ts test/tokens.test.ts test/audit.test.ts test/admin.test.ts
acceptance.expected: On the candidate, 0 fail in selected tests; a focused run may fail the global coverage threshold, whose gate is the full suite. Counterexamples 1-13 pass, with case 11 supplied by unchanged existing tests. Cases 1-2 reject inherited top-level elements with uptime[1]: must be an object, latency[1]: must be an object and uptime[0]: must be an object. Cases 3-4 reject nested inherited days at uptime[0].days[89], latency[0].days[89], uptime.days[89] and uptime[1].days[89] with is required. Holes, accessor elements/fields, inherited checkId, setter-only checkId and repeat validation after accessor/hole mutation have the exact Counterexamples 5-8 and 10 errors; all getter counts are 0. Enumerable Object.prototype.extra preserves validateComponent ok:true. Dense JSON, null-prototype items and non-enumerable own declared fields return ok:true with value identical to input. Existing own-data tests for unions, recursive JSON, record keys and non-plain prototypes remain green.

0 fail in selected tests; focused coverage is not the full-suite gate. Counterexample 13a-c each uses the JSON HTTP check with headers X-Key:v and Auth:{env:PULSE_HEADER_A}. Non-enumerable Object.prototype constructor getter, arrow constructor plus prototype getter, and hasOwnProperty getter each yield ok:true, value === c and count === 0. Restore every saved prototype descriptor in finally, deleting only properties newly added by the test. These tests must exercise the exported validateCheck, not private walk helpers.

Review against Required behavior 1-5: schema-cached compiled walks, no trust cached by input, no input copies or per-value allocation at object/array schemas, and only the two record key arrays permitted per record value. Descriptor-only record globals checking runs at most once per problem call and only when reached, comparing constructor and hasOwnProperty to module-load originals; records with any own constructor or unsafe globals fall back to the copy. Preserve all prototype, own-data, setter, absent-key/inherited-key, union, lazy and enumerable-Object.prototype rules. arrayProblem uses ownValue(value,i), preserving its accessor error. The sole removed assertions belong to the named descriptor/get Proxy test, replaced with no-throw and typeof result.ok === boolean checks for every original validator call; hostile-trap and cyclic-prototype tests stay unchanged.

acceptance.command: git diff 7ce23aaf3fa3e038f65ecfed755188b83bde143f -- docs/index.md README.md package.json test/validate.bench.test.ts && node -p "require('./package.json').version"
acceptance.expected: The version prints 1.7.1. Validators and Error format docs state that array elements at every level count only as own data and that Proxy inputs are out of scope; validators still never throw and preserve input identity. README is changed only if it repeats those rules; the bench test is changed only for the optional shared-fixture move. No consumer pin update or api benchmark budget change.

exit 0 on the final candidate: lint (including cognitive complexity <= 15), build, TypeScript 7 typecheck covering src and test, and the full test suite with line coverage >= 0.8. No threshold or configuration weakening. Counterexamples 1-13, own-data tests and package export/type/dist smoke tests all pass; test/validate-cpu.ts is linted/typechecked but is not discovered as a test.

acceptance.command: bun run build && git diff --exit-code -- dist
acceptance.expected: exit 0 after committing the regenerated dist files; an independent build matches committed output.

acceptance.command: bun --version && uname -a && lscpu && git -C "$CONTRACT_A_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD && git -C "$CONTRACT_B_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD && git -C "$CONTRACT_MAIN_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD && for root in "$CONTRACT_A_ROOT" "$CONTRACT_B_ROOT" "$CONTRACT_MAIN_ROOT"; do (cd "$root" && bun install --frozen-lockfile) || exit; done
acceptance.expected: Prepare disposable worktrees on the same machine: CONTRACT_A_ROOT is ebcbbb613328494185833f7133f1242910986948, CONTRACT_B_ROOT is the final candidate PR-head SHA, and CONTRACT_MAIN_ROOT is 7ce23aaf3fa3e038f65ecfed755188b83bde143f. All three installations exit 0 using their lockfiles and Bun 1.4.0. Record resolved full SHAs, exact setup commands, Bun version, OS and CPU model in the PR.

acceptance.command: for round in 1 2 3; do bun "$CONTRACT_B_ROOT/test/validate-cpu.ts" "$CONTRACT_A_ROOT" || exit; bun "$CONTRACT_B_ROOT/test/validate-cpu.ts" "$CONTRACT_B_ROOT" || exit; done
acceptance.expected: All 6 fresh processes exit 0, ordered A,B,A,B,A,B, using the identical candidate script against each root/src/index.ts. The script narrows imported validators from unknown without any; each fixture is JSON-parsed before timing and has 1000 checks x 90 days from 2026-01-01 with the literal uptime/latency values in CPU statistic. Assert ok:true and value === input before timing, then 2 warmups and 7 process.cpuUsage user+system samples per workload. Each process prints one JSON line {root,bun,uptime:{samples,median},latency:{samples,median}}; median is the 4th-smallest sample. Per workload, side values are the 2nd-smallest of 3 invocation medians. Using unrounded values, B <= 1.10 * A for both workloads. Report all 3x7 raw samples per side/workload, invocation medians, side values rounded to 0.01 ms and (B/A-1)*100 rounded to 0.1%; keep the 10% bound and all safety checks.

acceptance.command: for round in 1 2 3; do bun "$CONTRACT_B_ROOT/test/validate-cpu.ts" "$CONTRACT_MAIN_ROOT" || exit; bun "$CONTRACT_B_ROOT/test/validate-cpu.ts" "$CONTRACT_B_ROOT" || exit; done
acceptance.expected: All 6 fresh processes exit 0 using the same CPU method. Report the additional A/B of today's main 7ce23aa against the candidate, with samples, medians and percentage changes; this comparison is evidence of the gain and is not the gating baseline.

PR body contains Completion evidence: test-first failures on 7ce23aa for 1-2; full-suite historical-walk failures for 3,4,9,11,13 compared with the specified list (including 13a-c count 1); guards 5-8,10,12 passing on 7ce23aa; final green test names/commands and bun run check output; name of the sole replaced Proxy test; both CPU A/Bs with exact commands, full SHAs, machine/Bun details, raw samples and derived statistics. Record findings for all applicable Security impact items (input validation, accessor/function execution, unchanged errors without secrets) and hostile inputs: polluted Object/Array prototypes, record constructor/prototype/hasOwnProperty variants and own constructor keys, frozen/subclass arrays, null-prototype objects and hostile Proxies. State known limits: disagreeing Proxy traps are out of scope but never throw, existing propertyIsEnumerable pollution behavior is not fixed and gains reach consumers only on their later pin updates. No compose or service startup check applies to this library-only change.
